chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who slandered his wife with adultery, and she is mute, deaf, not hearing what he said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she has proof (witnesses), so they testify in the presence of the Imam, he is whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and they are separated between the two of them, then she is not permissible for him forever; and if there is no proof, so she is prohibited unto him for as long as he stays with her, and there is no sin upon her from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man slanders his mute wife with adultery and she has no witnesses?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuances of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) when the wife is mute and deaf, distinguishing between cases with external witnesses versus those relying on the husband's oath. It highlights the Shia juristic view that if she lacks witnesses, the separation is temporary contingent on cohabitation, contrasting with the permanent separation in the witnessed scenario. This reflects the practical application of Quranic principles in family law, emphasizing the preservation of lineage and marital rights.
